Overview

Task Tracker v1.0.0

Shipped by the Antech /ship agent team for CEO Nageshwar.

Create tasks with a title, notes, due date and priority, mark them done and filter by status - in the browser or on Android. The Android app stores everything in the phone's internal storage, works fully offline and syncs with the server when you tap Sync.

PartTechnologyLocation
REST APIJava 21, Spring Boot 4.1.2, Spring Data JPA, H2 (dev) / PostgreSQL (prod), springdocbackend/
Web UIVanilla HTML, CSS, JavaScript (fetch) served by the APIbackend/src/main/resources/static/
Android appNative Java, SQLite in internal storage, HttpURLConnection syncandroid/
ShipmentExecutable JAR + APKdist/ and the GitHub Release task-tracker-v1.0.0

Run it

Executable JAR (Java 17+ required, 21 recommended)

java -jar dist/task-tracker-1.0.0.jar

Open http://localhost:8080 for the web UI and http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html for the API docs. Data is kept in ./data/ (H2 file database) in the folder you start it from.

Production (PostgreSQL)

SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod DB_URL=jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/tasks DB_USERNAME=tasks DB_PASSWORD=... \
APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://tasks.example.com JPA_DDL_AUTO=update java -jar dist/task-tracker-1.0.0.jar
VariableDefaultPurpose
PORT8080HTTP port
SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVEdevdev = H2 file DB, prod = env-configured database
DB_URL, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD-Database connection (prod)
APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINShttp://localhost:8080Comma-separated origins allowed to call the API
JPA_DDL_AUTOupdate (dev), validate (prod)Schema management. Use update on the first prod start

Android APK

Install the APK from the GitHub Release (task-tracker-1.0.0-debug.apk, or task-tracker-1.0.0.apk when signing secrets are configured):

adb install task-tracker-1.0.0-debug.apk

Or copy it to the phone and open it (allow "Install unknown apps" for your file manager). To sync, open the menu, choose Server URL, enter your server address, then tap Sync. Release builds require https://. Debug builds on the emulator default to http://10.0.2.2:8080.

Where the data lives: /data/data/com.antech.tasktracker/databases/task-tracker.db and private shared preferences. Only the app can read them. The app requests no storage permission, and Android backup and device transfer are excluded, so the data stays on the phone until the app is uninstalled.

Build from source

cd backend && ./mvnw test && ./mvnw package     # JAR in backend/target/
cd android && gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.10.2 && ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug

The Android build needs the Android SDK (ANDROID_HOME). Without it, push a tag task-tracker-v*: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/task-tracker-ci.yml) builds the JAR and APK and attaches them to the release.

Quick Start Guide

Quick Start Guide - Task Tracker v1.0.0

This guide takes you from download to a working Task Tracker on your computer and your Android phone, one step at a time. No programming knowledge is needed.

What you get

PartWhat it does
Task Tracker server (task-tracker-1.0.0.jar)Stores tasks and serves the web app at http://localhost:8080
Web appCreate, complete, filter and delete tasks in any browser
Android app (task-tracker-1.0.0-debug.apk)The same tasks on your phone. Works without internet, keeps all data in the phone's internal storage, syncs when you tap Sync

Before you start

You need:

  1. A Windows, macOS or Linux computer with Java 17 or newer. To check, open a terminal (Windows: press Win + R, type cmd, press Enter) and run java -version. If it says "not recognized" or shows a version below 17, install the free Eclipse Temurin 21 from https://adoptium.net and open a new terminal.
  2. For the mobile app: an Android phone with Android 8.0 or newer, and a USB cable or another way to copy a file to the phone.
  3. The release files from GitHub: https://github.com/naddanki87/antechsolutions/releases/tag/task-tracker-v1.0.0

Step 1 - Download the files

  1. Open the release page above.
  2. Under Assets, download task-tracker-1.0.0.jar (the server) and task-tracker-1.0.0-debug.apk (the Android app). SHA256SUMS.txt lets you check that the downloads are intact (optional, see Step 9).
  3. Create a folder, for example C:\TaskTracker, and move task-tracker-1.0.0.jar into it.

Step 2 - Start the server

  1. Open a terminal in the folder. On Windows: open the folder in File Explorer, click the address bar, type cmd and press Enter.
  2. Run: ``bash java -jar task-tracker-1.0.0.jar
  3. Wait until the last lines include Started TaskTrackerApplication. This takes about 10 seconds.
  4. Leave this window open. Closing it stops Task Tracker. Your tasks are saved in a data folder next to the JAR and are still there the next time you start it.

If you see Port 8080 was already in use, start it on another port instead: java -jar task-tracker-1.0.0.jar --server.port=8090 and use 8090 instead of 8080 in the next steps.

Step 3 - Use the web app

  1. Open a browser and go to http://localhost:8080.
  2. Add a task: type a Title (required), optionally choose a Due date and a Priority (Low, Medium, High) and add Notes, then click Add task.
  3. Complete a task: tick the checkbox next to it. The title is struck through. Untick to reopen it.
  4. Filter: use All, Open or Done above the list.
  5. Delete: click Delete next to a task.

If the page shows an error such as "Title is required", correct the field and click Add task again.

Step 4 - Install the Android app

  1. Copy task-tracker-1.0.0-debug.apk to your phone (USB cable, Google Drive, email to yourself, ...).
  2. On the phone, open the file (for example in Files > Downloads).
  3. Android asks to allow installing apps from this source: tap Settings, turn on Allow from this source, go back and tap Install.
  4. If Google Play Protect warns about an unknown app, tap More details > Install anyway. This appears because this test build is not signed for the Play Store.
  5. Open Task Tracker from the app drawer.

Developers can install from a computer instead: adb install task-tracker-1.0.0-debug.apk.

Step 5 - Use the app offline

The app works without any server or internet connection:

  1. Tap Add task, fill in the title, notes, due date (tap the date button) and priority, then tap Save.
  2. Tap a task to edit it, tick Done, or tap Delete.
  3. Tick the checkbox in the list to complete a task quickly.
  4. Use All / Open / Done at the top to filter.

Tasks you have not synced yet show "not synced" under the title. They are already saved on the phone.

Where your data is stored: in the app's private internal storage (/data/data/com.antech.tasktracker/databases/task-tracker.db). Other apps cannot read it, it is not copied to cloud backups, and it is removed only when you uninstall the app.

Step 6 - Sync the phone with the server (optional)

Sync shares tasks between the phone and the web app.

  1. Find your computer's address on your Wi-Fi network. On Windows run ipconfig and look for IPv4 Address, for example 192.168.1.20. The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi.
  2. The app only sends tasks over secure https:// connections. The single exception is the Android emulator, which reaches your computer at http://10.0.2.2:8080 (already preset in this test build). For a real phone, publish the server behind HTTPS (see Step 8), or use a tunnelling tool that gives you an https:// address for http://localhost:8080. A plain http://192.168... address is blocked by Android and shows "Offline".
  3. In the app, open the menu (⋮, top right) > Server URL, enter the https:// address and tap OK.
  4. Tap Sync. You see "Synced: N sent, M received". Tasks created in the web app now appear on the phone, and phone tasks appear in the web app after you refresh the page.
  5. Without a connection you see "Offline - changes are saved on this device". Nothing is lost; tap Sync again later.

If the same task was changed in both places, the server's version is kept and the phone updates to match.

Step 7 - Explore the API (for developers)

  • Interactive API documentation: http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html
  • Health check: http://localhost:8080/actuator/health (shows "status":"UP")
  • Example: ``bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title":"First task","priority":"HIGH"}'

See the API Reference section for every endpoint.

Step 8 - Run it for a team (production)

  1. Create a PostgreSQL database and user.
  2. Start the server with production settings (one line): ``bash SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod DB_URL=jdbc:postgresql://db-host:5432/tasks DB_USERNAME=tasks DB_PASSWORD=your-password APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://tasks.example.com JPA_DDL_AUTO=update java -jar task-tracker-1.0.0.jar ` On Windows cmd, set each variable first with set NAME=value, then run java -jar task-tracker-1.0.0.jar`.
  3. Put it behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (for example Nginx, Caddy or a cloud load balancer) so phones can sync.
  4. After the first start, set JPA_DDL_AUTO=validate.
  5. Note: v1.0.0 has no login. Run it only on a trusted network or behind a proxy that requires sign-in until v1.1 adds authentication (see the Security Report, SEC-4).

Step 9 - Verify your downloads (optional)

On Windows PowerShell:

Get-FileHash task-tracker-1.0.0.jar -Algorithm SHA256

On macOS/Linux: shasum -a 256 task-tracker-1.0.0.jar. The value must match the line in SHA256SUMS.txt.

Troubleshooting

ProblemFix
'java' is not recognizedInstall Java 21 (Before you start, item 1) and open a new terminal
Unsupported class file major version / UnsupportedClassVersionErrorJava is older than 17. Install Java 21
Port 8080 was already in useAdd --server.port=8090 and use port 8090
Web page does not loadMake sure the terminal from Step 2 is still open and shows Started TaskTrackerApplication
Android: "App not installed"Uninstall an older Task Tracker first, then install again
Android: "Use an https:// address"Release builds only accept https:// server addresses (Step 6)
Android: "Offline - changes are saved on this device"Check Wi-Fi and the Server URL; the server must be running, reachable and use https:// (Step 6)
Android: "Sync failed: ..."The server rejected a change; open the task, check the title (max 120 characters), save and sync again

Stop and uninstall

  • Stop the server: press Ctrl + C in its terminal, or close the window.
  • Remove server data: delete the data folder next to the JAR.
  • Remove the app: long-press Task Tracker > Uninstall. This also deletes all tasks stored on the phone.
Specification

Task Tracker - Specification (Spec)

Requirement (CEO Nageshwar): Task tracker: users create tasks with a title, notes, due date and priority, mark them done, and filter by status. The Android app works fully offline and syncs when online.

Scope

  • Single-tenant, no login in v1.0.0 (Armor-approved: no personal data beyond task text; auth is a v1.1 item).
  • Web UI served by the backend; Android app is local-first with optional sync.

Domain model - Task

FieldTypeRules
idUUIDServer-generated on POST; client-generated on PUT (offline create)
titlestringrequired, 1-120 chars after trim
notesstring?max 1000 chars
dueDatedate? (yyyy-MM-dd)optional
priorityenum LOW, MEDIUM, HIGHdefault MEDIUM
donebooleandefault false
deletedbooleansoft delete flag, only visible in /changes
versionlongoptimistic locking; stale -> 409
createdAt, updatedAtISO-8601 UTC instantserver-managed

User stories and acceptance criteria

  • US-1 Create task. AC-1: valid POST returns 201, Location header and the task with done=false, priority=MEDIUM when omitted, version=0. AC-2: blank title or title > 120 chars returns 400 ProblemDetail with a title field error.
  • US-2 List and filter. AC-3: GET /tasks returns a page sorted by createdAt desc by default, excluding deleted tasks. AC-4: ?done=true|false filters by status. AC-5: size above 100 is clamped to 100.
  • US-3 View task. AC-6: GET /tasks/{id} returns 200; unknown or deleted id returns 404.
  • US-4 Update / complete. AC-7: PUT with the current version updates and returns 200 with version+1. AC-8: PUT with a stale version returns 409. AC-9: PUT on an unknown id creates it (201) - offline create. AC-10: PUT on a deleted task returns 409.
  • US-5 Delete. AC-11: DELETE returns 204 and the task disappears from list/get; unknown id returns 404.
  • US-6 Sync. AC-12: GET /tasks/changes?since=<instant> returns all tasks (incl. deleted) with updatedAt > since, oldest first.
  • US-7 Android offline. AC-13: the app creates, edits, completes and deletes tasks with no network, storing them in internal storage only. AC-14: "Sync" pushes local changes and pulls server changes; network failure keeps local data and shows "Offline".
  • US-8 Web. AC-15: the web page lists tasks with a status filter, creates tasks, toggles done and deletes, showing loading, empty and error states.

Android local storage (agreed with Swift)

Table tasks in task-tracker.db (app-private databases dir) mirrors the model plus dirty. Settings (API base URL, last pull time) in private SharedPreferences. No storage permissions, backups excluded.

Contract

See openapi.yaml.

API Reference

Task Tracker API reference (Scribe)

Base URL: http://localhost:8080/api/v1. JSON in and out. Errors are RFC 7807 application/problem+json:

{ "type": "https://antech.dev/problems/validation", "title": "Validation failed", "status": 400,
  "detail": "One or more fields are invalid", "instance": "/api/v1/tasks",
  "errors": [ { "field": "title", "message": "must not be blank" } ], "timestamp": "2026-10-30T10:15:30Z" }

Problem types: validation (400), malformed-request (400), request-error (other 4xx), not-found (404), conflict (409), internal (500, includes correlationId).

Task object

{
  "id": "3f2b8c1e-6a1d-4f0e-9a43-0f5c2b7d9e11",
  "title": "Pay invoices",
  "notes": "Supplier batch",
  "dueDate": "2026-11-05",
  "priority": "HIGH",
  "done": false,
  "deleted": false,
  "version": 0,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-30T10:15:30Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-30T10:15:30Z"
}

List tasks - GET /tasks

Query: done (true/false, optional), page (0..), size (1-100, larger values are clamped), sort (default createdAt,desc).

curl "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks?done=false&size=20&sort=dueDate,asc"

200 { "content": [Task...], "page": 0, "size": 20, "totalElements": 3, "totalPages": 1 } · 400 unknown sort field.

Create a task - POST /tasks

Body: title (required, max 120), notes (max 1000), dueDate (yyyy-MM-dd), priority (LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH, default MEDIUM).

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Pay invoices","dueDate":"2026-11-05","priority":"HIGH"}'

201 + Location: /api/v1/tasks/{id} + Task · 400 validation.

Get a task - GET /tasks/{id}

curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks/3f2b8c1e-6a1d-4f0e-9a43-0f5c2b7d9e11

200 Task · 404 unknown or deleted · 400 id is not a UUID.

Update or create - PUT /tasks/{id}

Body: the create fields plus done and version. Send the version you last read; it is ignored when the id does not exist yet (offline create).

curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks/3f2b8c1e-6a1d-4f0e-9a43-0f5c2b7d9e11 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Pay invoices","priority":"HIGH","done":true,"version":0}'

200 updated (version + 1) · 201 created · 409 stale version or task deleted · 400 validation.

Delete - DELETE /tasks/{id}

curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks/3f2b8c1e-6a1d-4f0e-9a43-0f5c2b7d9e11

204 · 404 unknown. Deletes are soft so sync clients can learn about them.

Sync feed - GET /tasks/changes?since=<instant>

Returns up to 500 tasks (including deleted ones) changed after since, oldest first. Repeat with the last updatedAt until fewer than 500 come back.

curl "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks/changes?since=2026-10-30T00:00:00Z"

200 { "content": [Task...] } · 400 missing or invalid since.

Operations

  • GET /actuator/health -> {"status":"UP"}
  • GET /v3/api-docs (OpenAPI JSON) and /swagger-ui.html
Architecture Decisions

Architecture decisions and agent handoffs (Scribe)

The complete, timestamped agent conversation is in ../.ship/events.jsonl and can be replayed in Antech Mission Control.

Decisions

#DecisionWhyOwner
D1UUID ids, client-generated allowed via PUT /tasks/{id}Android creates tasks offline without id collisionsSpec + Swift
D2Optimistic locking with version; stale -> 409, server winsSimple, lossless conflict rule for two clientsSpec + Byte
D3Soft delete + /changes?since= feedSync clients must learn about deletionsSpec + Swift
D4Sync checkpoint = last server updatedAt, not the device clockAvoids clock-skew gapsSwift
D5markSynced only clears dirty when updated_at is unchangedAn edit made during an upload is never lostSwift
D6Android uses framework SQLite + HttpURLConnection, no Room/RetrofitSmall APK, no third-party code, internal storage onlySwift
D7No authentication in v1Single tenant, no personal data; planned for v1.1 (SEC-4)Spec + Armor
D8Spring Boot 4.1.2 (Initializr default) + springdoc 3.2.0Current supported lineByte
D9Stable PageResponse DTO instead of serializing Spring's PageContract stays stable across Spring versionsByte
D10APK built in GitHub ActionsNo Android SDK on the build machine; CI is reproducibleDeployer

Handoffs

  1. CEO -> Spec: requirement. Spec -> Byte, Swift, Armor: contract review, all approved (Gate 1).
  2. Byte, Pixel, Swift implemented in parallel against openapi.yaml (Gate 2).
  3. Armor -> Byte: SEC-1, SEC-2 (500 on bad input), SEC-6 (generated password in log). Byte fixed all three and updated the /ship skill templates so future products inherit the fixes.
  4. Hawk -> Byte: build failure (PropertyReferenceException moved in Spring Data 4). Fixed, suite green (Gate 3).
  5. Scribe documented from the code; Deployer built, smoke-tested, committed, pushed and released (Gate 4).

Security Report

Security Report - Task Tracker v1.0.0

ProductTask Tracker v1.0.0 (REST API, web app, Android app)
AssessmentStatic code review, configuration review, automated security regression tests
AssessorArmor (security agent), report compiled by Scribe
Date2026-10-30
Commit assessedfeat/task-tracker, release tag task-tracker-v1.0.0
VerdictApproved for release. 0 Critical, 0 High open. 4 findings fixed, 2 Low risks accepted for v1

1. Executive summary

Task Tracker was reviewed against the OWASP Top 10 (2021) for the API and web app and the OWASP Mobile Top 10 for the Android app. Armor found four issues during development, all fixed before release: three caused server errors (HTTP 500) on bad input or exposed a generated password in the startup log, and one removed an unneeded database console component. Each fix has an automated regression test that runs on every build.

Two low risks are accepted for v1.0.0 by product scope: the API has no user login (single-team use, no personal data), and the debug Android build may talk to a local test server over plain HTTP. Adding authentication is the main recommendation for v1.1.

SeverityFoundFixedAcceptedOpen
Critical0000
High0000
Medium3300
Low3120

2. Scope

ComponentIn scope
Spring Boot REST API (backend/src/main/java)Controllers, services, repository, validation, error handling, security configuration
Configuration (application.yml, pom.xml)Profiles, secrets handling, actuator, CORS, dependencies
Web app (static/index.html, app.js, styles.css)XSS, script sources, data handling
Android app (android/app)Data storage, permissions, network security, backups, exported components, SQL
Build and CI (.github/workflows/task-tracker-ci.yml)Secrets handling, signing, supply chain

Out of scope: infrastructure hosting, penetration testing of a deployed instance, and the Android UI on physical devices.

3. Method

  1. Contract review in the architecture phase (data model, endpoints, sync design).
  2. Line-by-line review of all changed files against the checklist in the Security Audit Checklist section.
  3. Automated scans: secret patterns (password=, secret, api_key, private keys) across Java, YAML, JS, XML and Gradle files, and a search for unsafe DOM APIs (innerHTML, eval, document.write).
  4. Security regression tests in TaskApiIntegrationTest: badInputNeverReturns500, errorsDoNotLeakInternals, securityHeadersAndCors, run on every CI build.
  5. Startup log inspection for credentials.

4. Findings

SEC-1 - Unknown sort field caused a server error (Medium, fixed)

  • Where: GET /api/v1/tasks?sort=<field>
  • Issue: an unknown field name (for example sort=bogus,asc) reached the catch-all error handler and returned HTTP 500. Repeated 500s hide real faults, add noise to monitoring and reveal that input reaches the data layer unchecked.
  • Fix: GlobalExceptionHandler maps PropertyReferenceException to 400 malformed-request.
  • Verification: badInputNeverReturns500 asserts 400; smoke test on the shipped JAR returned 400.

SEC-2 - Missing or invalid parameters caused server errors (Medium, fixed)

  • Where: GET /api/v1/tasks/changes without since, unsupported content types and other framework errors.
  • Issue: these fell through to the catch-all handler and returned 500 instead of a 4xx status.
  • Fix: MissingServletRequestParameterException returns 400, and every Spring MVC error with a 4xx status (415, 405, 406...) keeps that status with a generic message.
  • Verification: badInputNeverReturns500 covers missing since, invalid since, non-UUID id, malformed JSON, unknown enum value and text/plain (415).

SEC-6 - Generated password written to the startup log (Medium, fixed)

  • Where: application startup.
  • Issue: Spring Boot created a default in-memory user and printed Using generated security password: ... to the log. Credentials in logs can leak through log shipping and support tickets.
  • Fix: SecurityConfig declares an empty InMemoryUserDetailsManager, so no default user or password exists.
  • Verification: test logs searched after the fix: no generated password present.

SEC-3 - Unused database console dependency (Low, fixed)

  • Where: pom.xml (spring-boot-h2console, added by the project generator).
  • Issue: a web database console is a common attack target if accidentally enabled.
  • Fix: dependency removed; spring.h2.console.enabled: false.

SEC-4 - No authentication in v1.0.0 (Low, accepted)

  • Where: all /api/v1/** endpoints.
  • Issue: anyone who can reach the server can read and change tasks.
  • Why accepted: single-team scope agreed in the specification; tasks contain no personal or financial data.
  • Mitigation now: run on a trusted network or behind a reverse proxy that requires sign-in (Quick Start, Step 8).
  • Planned: login and per-user ownership checks in v1.1.

SEC-5 - Debug Android build allows HTTP to local test hosts (Low, accepted)

  • Where: android/app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml.
  • Issue: the debug build may send traffic unencrypted to 10.0.2.2 (emulator host) and localhost.
  • Why accepted: debug-only and limited to the two loopback test hosts; release builds allow HTTPS only, and the in-app Server URL setting rejects http:// in release builds.

5. Controls confirmed

AreaControl
Input validationBean Validation on every request body (@NotBlank, @Size), typed UUID, date, instant and enum binding
InjectionSpring Data derived queries only; Android SQL uses ContentValues and ? arguments
Error handlingRFC 7807 responses without stack traces, exception names or framework messages; 500s get a correlation id in the server log
Transport and headersCSP default-src 'self', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
CORSExplicit allow-list from APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; other origins get 403 (tested)
SecretsNone in the repository; production database and APK signing keys come from environment variables and GitHub secrets
ExposureOnly static files, API docs, /actuator/health and /actuator/info, and /api/v1/**; everything else denied
Abuse limitsPage size capped at 100, sync feed capped at 500 rows, field length limits
Web XSSAll data rendered with textContent; no inline scripts or event handlers; no third-party scripts
Mobile storageSQLite and settings in app-private internal storage; no storage permissions; backups and device transfer excluded
Mobile componentsOnly the launcher activity is exported; release builds minified with debug logs stripped
